description: Fix backend CORS headers, CSRF origin validation, and rate limiting to properly work behind the Cloudflare edge worker for auth endpoints.
steps: In apps/backend/app/main.py, add 'x-turnstile-token' and 'CF-Turnstile-Response' to the allow_headers list in the CORSMiddleware configuration (line 135). This ensures browser preflight requests succeed when these headers are sent.

In apps/backend/app/config.py, modify the allowed_origins_list property to also include pattern matching for Cloudflare Pages preview domains. Add logic that, in addition to the comma-separated ALLOWED_ORIGINS, also matches any origin of the form https://<hash>.syrabitfrontend.pages.dev. This can be done by adding a helper method or modifying the property to append dynamically.

In apps/backend/app/main.py unified_middleware, update the CSRF origin check to also allow origins that match the *.syrabitfrontend.pages.dev pattern. Alternatively, leverage the updated allowed_origins_list property from config.py since the CSRF check already uses settings.allowed_origins_list.

In apps/backend/app/api/v1/auth.py, modify the _check_rate_limit function to prefer the X-Real-IP or X-Forwarded-For header over request.client.host. The edge worker sets X-Real-IP with the actual user IP. Fallback to request.client.host if header is not present.

Add or update tests in apps/backend/tests/test_auth.py to verify: (a) CORS response includes x-turnstile-token in allowed headers (can test via OPTIONS request), (b) rate limiting uses X-Real-IP when available.
acceptance_criteria: CORS preflight response includes 'x-turnstile-token' and 'CF-Turnstile-Response' in Access-Control-Allow-Headers
Origins like https://d2136f37.syrabitfrontend.pages.dev are accepted by CSRF validation and CORS
Rate limiting in auth.py uses X-Real-IP header value when present instead of request.client.host
All existing backend tests pass plus new tests for the above
Python code has no import errors or syntax issues
findings: All 9 auth tests pass. 20 pre-existing failures in test_payment_lifecycle, test_security (SSRF), and test_webhook are unrelated (confirmed by running on base commit). The test_circuit_breaker tests also fail pre-existing due to missing pytest-asyncio. Installed dependencies manually since requirements.txt hash mode failed on Python 3.12.
